how: secret_store.rs keeps all secrets in one keyring entry (one OS prompt per process); BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY for harnessed agents is injected into the child env; sprig dev-MCP strips the key from its own env and re-materializes it as a 0600 keyfile for git helpers; egress_guard rejects ncryptsec1 material at 13 relay-bound boundaries with an inventory test that fails the build when a new /events URL site lacks the guard; provider_config rejects key names containing secret, password, token, key or credential; provider output is redacted; RESERVED_ENV_KEYS blocks user env from disabling safety knobs; K8s Secrets are per-attempt immutable and any principal with secret-read in the namespace can read the nsec (stated).
verevonRelevance: The inventory-completeness test that fails when a new egress path skips the guard is a transferable way to enforce a data-handling rule across a large codebase.
notes: Raw nsec intentionally transits the encrypted pairing session; raw-key DLP is marked as separate future work.

name: Supply-chain and deployment-identity controls
what: Relay images carry signed provenance and a deployment-eligibility attestation, toolchains are pinned, and dependency policy is enforced in CI.
how: Canonical images from ghcr.io/block/buzz have SLSA build provenance and a custom predicate recording the same-SHA CI run and Helm chart version; tags are created only after CI succeeds on the full SHA; /_status exposes build identity; Hermit pins rust, node, flutter, just, pgschema and others; cargo-deny (deny.toml), lefthook, security CI workflows and a codex security-review workflow; protected-branch release PRs with immutable candidates.
verevonRelevance: Gate promotion on attestations that bind an image digest to green CI for the same commit; Verevon release gates R-1..R-5 could be recorded as an attestation predicate.
notes: Slack and Teams cannot be compared here (closed source).

name: Operational telemetry with closed label sets and privacy-aware tracing
what: Metrics stay bounded in cardinality and never carry tokens, device ids or per-community series unless explicitly enabled.
how: Prometheus label values come from closed enums (APNs outcome classes, admission results, readiness causes); per-community usage metrics default off; leader-only DB gauges with availability gauges (absence is never zero); stale data keeps original age; buzz-datastore-tracing provides policy-enforcing macros for logical datastore spans; early startup emits fixed-schema JSON lifecycle events; DB pools export idle/active/max gauges per role; OTLP traces optional.
verevonRelevance: Adopt the rule "pair every aggregate gauge with an availability gauge so absence is not read as zero" and closed label vocabularies for Space metrics under ZDR.
notes: Purpose of the datastore tracing macros inferred from the crate header; medium confidence on exact policy.

name: Media authorization gap and what is absent: DLP, residency, SCIM, eDiscovery export
what: Blob reads need an authenticated host-scoped Blossom grant, but a read is not tied to the channel ACL of the message it was attached to; several enterprise compliance features are not present.
how: Per the conformance table, GET/HEAD /media/{sha256.ext} requires a Blossom t=get auth event scoped to the host or blob hash and binds to the header-resolved tenant, so relay membership plus a known hash is sufficient (gap deferred). No DLP, data-residency controls, SCIM or compliance export were found (grep and doc review); retention exists as event TTL refresh for ephemeral channels, observer ephemerality and local archive retention; VISION claims eDiscovery works because content is server-managed.
verevonRelevance: Verevon deny-by-default effect policies with retention_class and residency fields are ahead here; do not copy blob access that bypasses room ACL.
notes: Absence claims are inference from greps over crates and docs; confidence medium. Slack and Teams offer DLP/eDiscovery/SCIM; Buzz does not.

name: Community as tenant selected by URL, with operator-provisioned lifecycle
what: A workspace is a URL; one relay can host one community or thousands; an operator can provision, archive, unarchive, transfer and delete communities.
how: communities table (host, signing key, icon, deletion state and fence generation) is the operator-global registry; requests bind to a community by Host; operator endpoints /operator/communities (provision, archive, unarchive, delete, transfer, availability) are NIP-98 signed by operator keys; archived or deleting communities disconnect live sockets; hosted community limit raised to fifty per user in v0.5.28; workspace icon via NIP-WP kind 9033 served through NIP-11.
verevonRelevance: Verevon orgs and Spaces map to communities and channels; the explicit operator lifecycle (archive before delete, transfer) is a useful reference for Space lifecycle states.
notes: Shared channels across communities do not exist; identity is portable but each community stores its own profile and DMs.

name: Portable key identity with per-community profile and per-host NIP-05
what: One keypair works in every community, but profile, DMs and presence live per community, so joining a second community leaks nothing about the first.
how: users PK is (community_id, pubkey); NIP-05 handles must canonicalize to the connected host and are unique per community; kind 0 is reposted per community; DMs, presence and memberships do not bleed across hosts; agents keep the same rule (VISION_AGENT).
verevonRelevance: Verevon identity is Control-issued, but the per-tenant profile rule is worth keeping for agents that serve several orgs.
notes: Key loss is unrecoverable by design; the vision docs list this as an honest cost.

name: Membership, roles and add-policy model: open and private channels, guests, bots, signed roster
what: Channels are open or private; roles are owner, admin, member, guest, bot; people and agents can limit who may add them; relay-level membership is a signed roster.
how: channel_members with soft delete (removed_at) and transactional role enforcement (TOCTOU-safe), NIP-29 commands 9000-9022, users.channel_add_policy, relay_members plus pubkey_allowlist, NIP-43 admin kinds 9030-9033 and relay-signed roster kind 13534 (published by buzz-admin), stateless invite codes minted and claimed over NIP-98 with terms acceptance, identity archival (NIP-IA) that hides retired keys from active surfaces without deleting history.
verevonRelevance: Verevon room roles are fixed to editor today; the guest role, soft-deleted membership and archival-without-deletion semantics are worth adopting.
notes: Guest is a role, not a separate external-sharing model; there are no shared channels between communities.

name: Ephemeral channels with a sliding TTL deadline
what: A channel can auto-archive after a period of inactivity, which suits short-lived rooms such as huddles and agent task rooms.
how: channels.ttl_seconds and ttl_deadline; a deferred trigger refresh_channel_ttl_after_event_insert pushes the deadline forward on every durable event (shared advisory lock so permanent-channel commits do not serialize; TTL transitions take it exclusively); kind 9002 ttl tag sets or clears (empty clears) and is validated; a reaper archives expired channels; huddle backing channels use ttl 3600.
verevonRelevance: Verevon case or task Spaces could expire automatically after inactivity, with deletion receipts handled by the existing saga.
notes: Best-effort refresh (a failure to refresh never rejects the event).

name: Huddles: WebSocket Opus relay with no SFU, peer-index epochs and owner-pod routing
what: Channel members join voice rooms hosted by the relay; participants on different pods still hear each other.
how: WS /huddle/{ephemeral_channel_id}/audio with NIP-42 auth and membership check; protocol v2 frames: 8-byte header (seq u16, 48 kHz timestamp u32, level dBov i8, flags u8) plus opaque Opus; relay prefixes a peer index (v3 adds an epoch byte); rooms cap at 25 peers (N x (N-1) copies per 20 ms tick) with a 255-value index pool rotated to avoid reuse; bounded drop-on-full audio channels and a never-dropping control channel; cross-pod rooms use the owner pod via the fenced mesh; recording and per-track publishing are reserved but not built; no video and no screen share.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no calls; a relay-forwarded Opus room is cheap but quadratic and has no video; weigh buying an SFU instead.
notes: The scale ceiling (25 peers) is explicit. Slack and Teams offer video, screen share and recording; Buzz does not. Code check: CURRENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION is 3 and the relay accepts any version from 1 to 3; the mesh wire comment says client frames are NIP-44 encrypted between endpoints, but no encryption code exists in audio/ or the desktop huddle module (grep), so treat huddle media as relay-readable Opus.

name: Huddle as an ephemeral private channel with lifecycle events and persistent record
what: Voice sessions carry their own chat, reactions and transcript in a private auto-expiring channel linked from the parent channel by start and end events.
how: Creator-signed kinds 48100 started and 48103 ended in the parent channel reference a private stream backing channel created with kind 9007 and ttl=3600; the relay validates that the signer created an active private ephemeral stream with the expected TTL; participant joined/left (48101/48102) are relay-emitted; reactions are ephemeral kind 24810 scoped to the backing channel; the last human leaving ends the huddle and archives the backing channel atomically; mobile reconstructs the visible card from parent-channel history.
verevonRelevance: Model a meeting as an ephemeral child Space with TTL and start/end markers in the parent; transcript, chat and agent notes then inherit room authorization and expiry.
notes: No AI recap or recording exists yet; transcripts are published as messages by participants desktops.

name: Agent voice participation runs on the owner desktop (local STT and TTS)
what: Agents can be added to a huddle and speak with locally synthesized voices; humans are transcribed locally.
how: Desktop huddle module: Opus with NetEq-style jitter buffer, VAD (earshot) with a 300 ms silence flush, sherpa-onnx STT and Pocket TTS models downloaded on demand; agent TTS publishers authenticate as the agent using its managed key and push audio into the same relay room; transcription publishes text events; push-to-talk global shortcut. Because synthesis and capture run in the owner desktop pipeline, agent voice depends on that machine being online (inference from the publisher design).
verevonRelevance: A path to Grok-style voice without server GPUs, but it ties agent speech to a user device; Verevon would more likely use cloud realtime voice already present for AI voice.
notes: Dependence on the owner desktop is my inference from agent_tts_publisher loading the managed agent key locally.

name: Agent-first CLI and Rust SDK crates as the extensibility surface
what: Everything a human can do in the app is scriptable by JSON-in/JSON-out CLI, and Rust crates expose typed event builders and a WebSocket client for bots.
how: buzz-cli command groups (agents, messages, channels, canvas, reactions, emoji, gifs, dms, users, workflows, feed, social, notes, repos, projects, patches, issues, pr, media, upload, mem, pack, moderation) with structured JSON stdout, stderr errors and exit codes; buzz-sdk typed event builders; buzz-ws-client and buzz-test-client; countdown-bot example; two-tier auth (NIP-98 keypair, dev pubkey). No OpenAPI or GraphQL description of the HTTP/WS surface and no app directory.
verevonRelevance: A CLI over the public API is the cheapest way to let agents, CI and power users script Verevon Spaces; publish a machine-readable API description alongside it (Buzz does not).
notes: Marketplace, apps tab and slash-command registry are absent (inventory), so extensibility is code-level.

name: Workflow engine: YAML-as-code with evalexpr conditions, cron claims and unwired approvals
what: Channel-scoped automations fire on messages, reactions, schedules or webhooks and can call webhooks or post messages, with every step traced.
how: Definitions parsed with serde_yaml into tagged enums (4 triggers, 7 actions); conditions via evalexpr with registered string functions and a 100 ms timeout; single-pass templates; semaphore of 100 concurrent runs (no queueing, returns CapacityExceeded); cron loop ticks every 60 s and claims scheduled_for slots through a unique row (at-most-once across pods); relay ActionSink posts relay-signed messages carrying owner attribution; send_dm and set_channel_topic return NotImplemented; request_approval returns Suspended but the relay marks the run Failed (approval_not_supported) because token persistence and resume are not wired.
verevonRelevance: Mirror of a Verevon gap (granted approval does not resume the paused run): do not expose approval steps until suspend, persist-token and resume are one tested path.
notes: Still stubbed at HEAD 799cfd705 (confirms the scout concern). Slack Workflow Builder is richer; the code-as-YAML angle is the differentiator.

name: Persona packs and plugin manifests
what: Agent personas, skills and MCP/hook configuration can be bundled and shared as packs.
how: buzz-persona parses .persona.md files and a .plugin/plugin.json manifest (pack instructions, mcp_config, hooks_config, skills directory) with merge and validation; persona triggers (mentions, keywords, all_messages) and lifecycle hooks (on_start, on_stop, on_message); examples/meadow-core ships a three-agent pack (orchestrator plus workers).
verevonRelevance: A portable agent pack format (prompt, tools, hooks, skills) is useful if Verevon lets orgs share agent definitions between Spaces.
notes: Read crate module list and manifest names only; pack distribution is via relay catalog events (NIP-AP).

name: NIP-AR channel artifacts: revisioned typed records with CAS on prev
what: Tasks, project cards and similar records live in a channel with exact optimistic concurrency, soft delete and restore, and never count as chat.
how: Kind 45010 events carry a complete snapshot with ar, d (stable UUID), h (home channel), type (namespaced), title, op (create, update, move, delete, restore), prev and optional root; the relay advances the current revision atomically so competing edits cannot both succeed and timestamps never choose a winner; resubmitting an accepted event succeeds (no false conflict); redaction by kind 9005 withholds a revision but keeps its id valid as prev; revisions do not change unread, counts or notifications; channel read permission governs every artifact surface. Desktop UI is thin.
verevonRelevance: A clean model for Space tasks or notes: one authorization (the room) plus prev-CAS revisions and idempotent resubmission, distinct from chat counters.
notes: Uncommon among references where tasks are separate apps. UI maturity is low (few desktop files).

name: Per-channel canvas with writer-consistent head, conflict handling and history restore
what: Each channel has one shared document with history and restore, saved against the current head so concurrent edits do not silently clobber.
how: Kind 40100 canvas events with get/set/history/restore commands in desktop and CLI; saves set consistency:"strong" so the head precondition reads from the writer; desktop canvasConflict.ts, CanvasHistoryPanel and many canvas tests (refetch error recovery, rejected save reset, unverified save, restore pending guard).
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no Space canvas; a single versioned document per Space with strong-read head checks would be a small first artifact.
notes: Single-document-per-channel is simpler than Slack canvases or Teams Loop.

name: Git hosting over object storage with an atomic manifest pointer
what: The relay serves git smart HTTP for repositories without any persistent filesystem and signs pushes with the pusher Nostr key.
how: Pack objects are create-only and content-addressed; the current ref state is one manifest pointer updated by compare-and-swap (S3 conditional PUT); each request hydrates an ephemeral working tree from the manifest and drops it; policy hook endpoint /internal/git/policy enforces branch protection; git-sign-nostr (NIP-GS) and git-credential-nostr (NIP-98) integrate with standard git; proofs for durability ordering, manifest reconstruction and linearizability in TLA+ relative to three object-store axioms gated per backend.
verevonRelevance: Low relevance to Verevon rooms; the transferable idea is a stateless request path that rebuilds working state from content-addressed objects plus one CAS pointer.
notes: Peers (Slack, Teams) have no equivalent; qm and Grok Bot do not host git.

name: Branch-as-channel projects with NIP-34 patches, PRs and issues in the room
what: Creating a branch creates a channel where patches, CI results, review and the merge decision live and are archived as the record.
how: Projects (kind 30621) group repositories and channels; branch channels via project channel requests; patches 1617, pull requests 1618/1619, issues 1621 and statuses 1630-1633; merge and review actions are signed events; agents create PRs with a channel link back to the originating conversation; buzz:// entity links render preview cards.
verevonRelevance: Shows the conversation-as-record model: work objects and discussion share one authorization boundary (the room).
notes: Projects UI is preview-gated per preview-features.json; I did not audit the 218-file projects feature.

name: Blossom media storage on S3 with thumbnails, per-community prefixes and snapshot accounting
what: Uploads are content-addressed, validated, thumbnailed and accounted per community without scanning S3 on the relay.
how: PUT /media/upload and GET /media/{sha256.ext} (BUD-01/02) with Blossom auth events; buzz-media validates and processes images and video (blurhash, thumbnails, ISO-BMFF checks) and writes upload records with network attribution; bucket_index classifies keys and tenant prefixes; buzz-admin storage-snapshot publishes a complete Postgres snapshot that the relay reads to export storage gauges (relay-local scans removed); bundled Silo (MinIO fork) for local deployments.
verevonRelevance: Move storage accounting off the hot service into a snapshot worker with freshness gauges; Verevon documents-api could do the same for per-Space usage.
notes: Media read authorization gap noted in governance records.

name: Tauri 2 desktop shell with bundled sidecars, strict plugin set and CSP
what: A native desktop app wraps the web UI and ships the agent runtime binaries it needs.
how: Tauri 2 (single-instance with deep-link, window-state, dialog, updater, process, opener, global-shortcut, notification); externalBin bundles buzz-acp, buzz-agent, buzz-backend-kubernetes, buzz-dev-mcp, git-credential-nostr and buzz; overlay title bar, backgroundThrottling disabled; CSP default-src self with connect-src allowing https/http/wss/ws and custom buzz-media protocol; 377 unique Tauri commands (inventory). Desktop is excluded from the Cargo workspace and builds separately.
verevonRelevance: Verevon v3 is SolidJS plus a Rust gateway; bundling sidecars is only relevant if a desktop agent runtime is wanted.
notes: CSP allows broad network egress; the app relies on egress_guard for specific secrets rather than network allowlists.

name: Deep links with pending queues, entity links and invite codes
what: buzz:// links open a message, repo, project, PR or issue, join a community with an invite code and policy receipt, and survive cold start.
how: tauri-plugin-deep-link with single-instance forwarding; deep_link.rs keeps de-duplicated pending queues for community, navigation and entity links so links arriving before the UI is ready are not lost; ENTITY_LINK_HOSTS allowlist (repo, project, pr, issue); links interpreted against the current community; the CLI emits a link field that the base prompt tells agents to paste verbatim to render preview cards.
verevonRelevance: Cold-start-safe pending queues and a link field in agent tool output are small, cheap wins for Verevon room and approval deep links.
notes: Cross-community links are not resolved; links are app-only.

name: Release engineering: three independent lanes, immutable candidates, signed canary then promote
what: Desktop, relay and mobile ship on separate, auditable pipelines; auto-update is wired only in configured release builds.
how: Desktop: just release-desktop creates one deterministic candidate commit and PR, merge is the authorization event, auto-tag verifies PR identity and checks, signed/notarized macOS canary then promote-oss-desktop-release; Linux, Windows (unsigned) and macOS Intel canaries; relay: metadata PR and multi-arch image; mobile: immutable mobile-vX.Y.Z-rc.N tags to the private pipeline; tauri-plugin-updater is registered only under a buzz_updater_enabled cfg and endpoint/public key come from build env.
verevonRelevance: Immutable candidate PRs where the merge is the authorization event is a pattern for Verevon gated releases.
notes: Windows builds are unsigned and agent shell needs Git Bash (README), so Windows is second-class.

name: Multi-community workspace switching with cross-community unread observation
what: Users keep several communities (up to fifty hosted) in a rail, reorder them and see unread across all of them.
how: features/communities (relay set, storage, icon cache, mark-read, leave, unread observer), CommunityRail with drag sorting, communityViewTransition for animated switches, per-community theme (kind 30078) and rate-limit gate reset on switch, identity archive and shared identity settings; each community is a separate relay connection and cache scope keyed by (pubkey, relay).
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no cross-room unread; a rail with a separate observer per tenant keeps multi-org users from being overwhelmed.
notes: Per-community isolation means N sockets for N communities; fine at tens, expensive at hundreds.

name: Test architecture: e2e bridge with mock IPC, 189 Playwright files, review-proven standards
what: UI behaviour is tested end to end without a live relay, and tests must bind production seams and be falsifiable.
how: desktop/src/testing/e2eBridge* mocks Tauri IPC and relay subscriptions (history, search, custom harnesses); desktop/tests/e2e holds about 189 spec and helper files; TESTING.md states the review-proven rule (regression tests bind the production seam and fail when the guard is removed; table tests over full input spaces; scoped locators); Rust side uses nextest per crate with explicit lists because nothing runs cargo test --workspace; Postgres-backed contract and race tests run in a dedicated job; mutation witnesses for formal models.
verevonRelevance: Adopt the falsifiability rule for Verevon authority tests: every guard needs a test that fails when the guard is deleted.
notes: Mock-Tauri browser tests explicitly do not certify native relay TTL or substrate health (agent-availability doc).

name: Build-time overlays: internal-only features, preview flags and enterprise adapter configuration
what: The same codebase builds the public app and an internal app with extra features, and enterprise builds hard-wire trusted relay and identity-adapter settings.
how: desktop/src/protectedFeatures has internal.ts/internalUi.ts for the internal build and empty public.ts exports for OSS; preview-features.json gates workflows, projects, pulse, forum and agentManagedProfiles via an Experimental settings card; BUZZ_BUILD_ENTERPRISE_AUTH_RELAYS and _ADAPTER_BASE_URL (HTTPS or loopback only) decide which relays may use NIP-FI; BUZZ_THEME_NAME/BASE_THEME brand builds; LaunchDarkly evaluator in the relay for server flags.
verevonRelevance: Verevon effect policies already gate features per org; Buzz shows a build-level overlay (internal vs public) for features that should not ship to every customer.
notes: The personal agent Bestie is internal-only (defined in internal.ts; public list empty).

name: Single multicall binary (sprig) for deploy-anywhere agents
what: One small binary acts as buzz-acp, buzz-agent, buzz-dev-mcp, the CLI and the git helpers depending on how it is invoked.
how: sprig dispatches on argv[0] personality (symlinks) to buzz_acp, buzz_agent or buzz_dev_mcp (which also handles rg, tree and buzz); the same pattern gives git-credential-nostr and git-sign-nostr; Dockerfile.sprig and sprig workflows produce the image used as the Kubernetes agent body.
verevonRelevance: A single static agent-runtime binary simplifies Verevon sandbox images and cuts startup time.
notes: Image size claims ("megabytes") not verified.

name: Mobile client architecture: Flutter with shared cross-client rules and an age gate
what: iOS and Android clients follow written intent (offline first, responsive, do not lose drafts, do not trust relays) and shared rules with desktop for ordering, unread and autocomplete.
how: Flutter with hooks_riverpod, nostr, secure storage, biometrics, QR scanning, deep links, app badge, native media and an age-signal gate; features for channels, forum, home, activity, search, pulse, pairing, invites; VISION_MOBILE declares the persistent store derived from events and discardable, with pending/sent/failed send states, bounded background work and push opening to the right conversation from cold start.
verevonRelevance: The "do not trust the relay" principle (critical actions enforced locally) is relevant to Verevon mobile planning.
notes: Doc states not all intents are realized; mobile is "being wired up" in the README.

name: Shortcuts, tray and accessibility posture; no command palette or i18n
what: Power-user shortcuts and a tray with running agents exist; there is no command palette and the UI is English-only.
how: Global shortcuts via tauri-plugin-global-shortcut (push-to-talk Ctrl+Space), in-app shortcuts for search (Cmd+K), channel search (Cmd+F), new message, create channel, zoom, reload; tray menu with Running and Recent agent activity and an action queue; aria attributes in 416 desktop files and reduced-motion handling in 74 (counts from scout greps); no i18n library or message catalogs found in desktop, web, admin-web or mobile.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs i18n from the start (Norwegian users); Buzz shows the cost of retrofitting. A command palette is a missing table-stake relative to Slack and Teams.
notes: Counts and absence claims come from the scout inventory greps; I did not re-run them.

name: One event log, three lenses: Stream, Forum and Workflow with per-surface notification defaults
what: The same data can be read as fast chat, slow threaded discussion or structured automation traces, each with its own noise level.
how: VISION surface table: Home (personal feed), Stream (topic chat, mandatory topics to sub-replies), Forum (posts with flat replies), DMs (up to 9), Agents, Workflows (steps and approval gates), Search; channel types stream, forum, dm, workflow in the DB; auxiliary panels for threads, canvas and members; Home inbox with hidden-DM inbox.
verevonRelevance: A Space could offer a fast chat lens and a slow decision lens (approvals, handoffs) over the same authorized record instead of one flat stream.
notes: Pulse, Projects, Forum and Workflows are preview-gated in the desktop even though VISION says all seven surfaces ship.

name: Product-design principle: facts decide, timers are a last-resort backstop
what: Onboarding messages and agent kickoff should speak from observed state, not from stopwatches.
how: Post-mortem of the Welcome kickoff: three failure directions (wrong story, too loud, too quiet) share one root cause, the kickoff decides what to say from timers (60 s, 15 s, 90 s) and absence of evidence, then writes it permanently; the one fact-based check is failedAfterKickoff; the guidance is to invert so facts decide wording and timers only backstop; a rejected-approaches section lists what not to retry.
verevonRelevance: Applies directly to Verevon agent status and onboarding in Spaces: derive UI claims from facts (run state, presence) rather than elapsed time.
notes: Engineering culture artifact; the rejected-approaches register is itself a good practice.

name: Relay-signed projection events keep thin clients correct without a second API
what: Derived state that clients cannot compute from raw events (who is in a channel, which DMs a viewer hid, who is archived, how many replies a thread has, who is online right now) is served as ordinary signed events authored by the relay key, so any NIP-01 client can read it and a generic cache or verifier still works.
how: The relay holds a signing key (per community in multi-tenant mode) and emits addressable or snapshot events as side effects of accepted commands: NIP-29 group metadata, admins and members (39000, 39001, 39002; the members snapshot is re-published on membership change and reconciled for very large channels), NIP-43 membership roster (13534) plus deltas (8000, 8001), membership notices (44100, 44101; clients may not submit them), per-viewer DM visibility snapshot (30622), identity archival delta and list (8002, 8003, 13535), query-time window overlays (39005 thread summary, 39006 and 39007 bounds, never stored), channel summary (40901) and a bulk presence snapshot (40902, synthesized from Redis). Reader-authorization predicates (author-only, owner-only, p-gated) apply to these kinds exactly as to client events.
verevonRelevance: Verevon could publish Space roster, audience revision and presence as server-signed, versioned snapshots next to the transcript, so every client (browser, agent runner, future desktop) renders the same authority state instead of recomputing it.
notes: The cost is relay-signing-key custody (a compromised key forges roster state) and write amplification on large channels (hence the large-channel reconciliation path). Slack and Teams expose the same derived state through proprietary APIs; Buzz keeps it inside the event vocabulary.

name: Encrypted author-only reminders with relay-side due scheduling (NIP-ER)
what: A user can attach a private reminder to a message or write a standalone one; the relay surfaces it to that user at the due time without learning what it is about, and agents can be woken by stream reminders.
how: Kind 30300 addressable event, content NIP-44 encrypted to the author (target id or address, status pending, done or cancelled, private note); only d (random, at least 128 bits), not_before (decimal unix seconds) and alt are public. The events table has not_before and delivered_at columns and a partial index for undelivered due rows. A relay worker (buzz-db reminder store) selects the latest head per (community, pubkey, d) with not_before <= now and delivered_at NULL in archived-community-excluding batches, claims a row with a stamp before publishing and releases it if the publish fails; the due signal is an EVENT frame to the author live subscriptions only (author-only kind) and is explicitly not a delivery guarantee: clients dedupe, enforce not_before locally and run recovery queries. Stream reminder kind 40007 is in the default subscription set of the agent harness and in the feed needs-action query.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no Space notifications or scheduled send; a private due-time primitive whose payload the platform cannot read fits ZDR and doubles as a wake signal for scheduled agent work.
notes: Relay due-delivery is best-effort by design. Teams and Slack have reminders and scheduled messages but keep content readable to the vendor; here the relay learns only that a reminder is due. Scheduled send (kind 40006) is defined but has no UI or CLI verb.

name: Mentions bind a label to one exact public key; ambiguity blocks the send
what: An @mention notifies exactly the person or agent the author picked, even when two members share a display name, and a mention cannot silently turn into plain text that notifies nobody.
how: The composer keeps a label-to-pubkey map and publishes both readable @Name text and separate p tags. Selecting a second identity with the same name reserves a qualified label that includes the full key; manually typed names with several exact-key matches are rejected with an instruction to use the picker, and the draft is kept. Pasted mentions are bound only after the community own state vouches for the identity, guarded by occurrence, generation and trust fences, and sends await pending bindings (bounded) before extracting recipients. The CLI resolves @Name against current channel members and refuses to send on an unresolved, ambiguous or non-member name; narrative names must drop the @ because every mention notifies. Sending never changes membership.
verevonRelevance: Verevon person mentions are text only today; adopting exact-identity binding (a structured recipient list next to the text) is the prerequisite for mention notifications and for agent addressing that cannot be spoofed by a look-alike name.
notes: Documentation plus tests describe the contract; I confirmed the CLI behaviour in the base prompt and did not re-read the TypeScript hooks end to end (confidence high on the contract, medium on every code path).

name: Owned-agent invitation flow: ownership is not membership, and authorization is re-checked at publish time
what: When someone @mentions an agent they own that is not yet in the channel, the composer offers Invite (add, then send) or reference-only; a failed add, a revoked policy or a cancelled attempt keeps the draft and sends nothing.
how: Owned-agent discovery is seeded by an owner-signed kind 30177 coordinate and proven by the agent kind 0 profile carrying exactly one valid NIP-OA auth tag; owner policy that is invalid fails closed and cannot revive a legacy permission; membership comes only from the latest relay-signed kind 39002 snapshot so an owned agent can be discovered with empty channel ids. The picker and preparation phase may admit a non-member, but publication separately refreshes authorization for the exact eventual destination (including a newly created DM); cached picker evidence is never publication authorization. One synchronous pending latch and abort signal cover preparation, inventory, adds and publication; recovery of the captured text, media and exact mention refs is fenced by visit and revision so a late response cannot revive cancelled intent.
verevonRelevance: Verevon rooms need the same two-step gate when a user pulls an agent into a Space: discovery and invitation evidence must never double as authority, and the final Control decision must be minted for the exact destination at send time.
notes: The design deliberately admits that membership reads and message publication are not one atomic transaction. Heavy frontend machinery (cancellation latches, draft recovery) is the price of keeping intent visible.

name: Portable agent snapshots: secrets excluded by construction, optional memory levels, locked NIP-44 envelope
what: An agent definition (prompt, runtime, model, profile and optionally its memory) can be exported as a file or as an avatar PNG, shared, previewed and imported without carrying keys or machine-local paths.
how: buzz-agent-snapshot v1 manifest in .agent.json or in a PNG tEXt chunk; only explicit fields are copied into the definition so nsec, auth tag, env vars, relay URL, harness paths and runtime state are never serialized (asserted by tests); memory is opt-in at three levels (none, core, everything) and fetched through the owner-gated engram path derived from the resolved instance, never from the caller; locked cards wrap the manifest in a NIP-44 v2 envelope decryptable only by the owner key or the exact agent key (exact-endpoint lookup, no trial decryption, generic refusal text, pre-decrypt size caps, 10 MiB PNG ceiling checked on final bytes). Card art generation is a separate optional OpenAI call whose key never leaves Rust; team snapshots follow the same envelope.
verevonRelevance: A secret-free, versioned export format for Space agent bindings and definitions would let orgs move agents between Spaces and environments; copy the allowlist-by-construction rule and the locked-envelope option for private definitions.
notes: Trading-card minting is a delight feature; the engineering value is the exclusion-by-construction and fail-closed unlock. Zip bundles for skills are deferred to v2.

name: Identity exactness: a persona or relay-signed ownership claim is never an alias for another agent key
what: Opening a profile from a message, DM, mention or deep link always shows exactly that key; a stopped agent never redirects to a running sibling made from the same persona, and cloud or remote agents are labelled as not managed on this device without implying hosting.
how: The canonical profile resolver treats an explicit public key as exact for active, stopped, archived and relay-only keys; owner-signed kind 30177 persona_id and archive-request persona links are not identity aliases and grant no access to a local sibling controls; there is no synthetic secretless record; persona navigation is a separate representative-picking path. A shared provenance marker (not managed on this device) is computed from an exact-key lookup in successfully loaded local inventory, and is withheld on failed inventory, unknown owner or other people identities; the marker grants no membership, mention eligibility, availability or management capability. Ownership permits owner-scoped relay reads, not local management.
verevonRelevance: Matches the Verevon rule that visibility is not authority (ADR-0002): keep agent definition, binding and running instance as separate identities in the Space roster, resolve by exact subject id, and never infer permissions from a shared definition.
notes: A bug class (hidden redirects between sibling agents) was removed by deleting an exception path instead of adding another flag, which is the cheaper long-term fix.

name: Structured, escaped turn framing and a trust ladder for relay-delivered content
what: Every agent turn arrives in explicit semantic sections so the model can tell the current request from history, routing metadata and mid-turn merges, and content that came from the relay is treated as lower trust than the operator prompt.
how: prompt_framing wraps standing context and each incoming turn in paired tags (buzz-event or buzz-events with Content, Event ID, From, Kind, Time, Tags, Parsed; thread-context or conversation-context for history; context for authoritative channel and reply-destination metadata; new-message-arrived-while-you-were-working and new-request-supersedes-previous for steer and supersede merges); attribute values are escaped while bodies stay byte-for-byte visible so review UIs show what the model executes. The base prompt forbids discovering or using relay-backed skills unless the authorizing human names the skill and says that even then the content is untrusted input that cannot override higher-priority instructions; lifecycle hook output is JSON-encoded for prompt-injection safety and carries lower trust than system messages.
verevonRelevance: A fixed envelope for room turns (author, audience revision, current request versus history) is what Verevon Session Core needs once several authors can address one agent; copy the rule that routing metadata is authoritative and message bodies are not.
notes: This is a prompt-level mitigation, not an isolation boundary; the information-flow proposal in the same repo exists because prompt rules alone are not enough.

name: Authenticated, cacheable media for the webview via a custom scheme and a loopback proxy
what: Images and video in private channels load in the desktop webview even though every blob read needs a signed grant, seek correctly, and stay cached across channel switches.
how: A registered buzz-media: asynchronous URI scheme plus an axum loopback proxy rewrite media requests to the current relay base URL and attach a freshly minted per-request media GET authorization (the helper can only mint for the relay base, so a token cannot reach a third-party origin); Range requests are forwarded for video; a 401 or 403 on a range stream is retried once with a re-minted token because the strict federated-identity read token lives 60 s; content-addressed URLs let the relay send immutable one-year cache headers which are forwarded to the WebKit HTTP cache; non-range responses over 20 MiB are refused to avoid buffering whole videos; the proxy rejects cross-origin callers other than the Tauri origins.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon rooms gain attachments, keep browser credentials out of media URLs by proxying through the BFF with per-request authorization and immutable content-addressed caching.
notes: Pairs with the media authorization gap noted elsewhere: the proxy solves transport auth, not the missing tie between a blob read and the message channel ACL.

name: Deployment-wide admin console on its own host with operator and moderator tiers
what: A hosting operator gets a private dashboard for reports, feedback, communities, members, bans and timeouts across every community, served from the relay process but isolated from tenant hosts.
how: Configured by BUZZ_ADMIN_HOST (activates /api/admin/v1 plus the admin-web SPA from BUZZ_ADMIN_WEB_DIR); every request carries NIP-98 auth and the signer is resolved to Operator (RELAY_OPERATOR_PUBKEYS, relay_operators table with audit) or Moderator capabilities; the legacy static token mode was removed and a stale variable only warns; routes cover reports (detail, resolve, reopen, cancel), feedback status, operators CRUD, cross-community member search and lookup, event preview, restrictions, direct ban and timeout; the SPA path exemption from tenant host checks is host-qualified so the same path on a tenant host stays protected; the desktop has a matching Admin Console that can browse and moderate every community; admin actions run through an outbox with leases and claim tokens.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs an operator surface that is not a customer org: separate host, signed request auth, two privilege tiers and an audit row per action, especially while Space effect policies are deny-by-default.
notes: Operator and tenant planes share one process, so isolation relies on host qualification and middleware ordering rather than separate deployments. Admin audit lives in relay_operator_audit (migration 0039).

name: Two deployment profiles: GitOps-safe production chart and a bundled quickstart
what: The same relay runs from a one-command Docker Compose bundle on a VPS, a Helm quickstart with bundled Postgres, Redis and object storage for evaluation, or an HA production chart that never invents secrets.
how: Helm chart profiles selected by values: production requires an existing Secret, external Postgres, Redis and S3 endpoints and fails at helm template time through _validate.tpl when inputs are missing; chart-side randomly generated secrets are only safe under helm install because ArgoCD and Flux render with helm template where lookup is empty, so the chart refuses that path for production; quickstart bundles Postgres, Redis and Silo (a MinIO fork) with a bucket-init job and autogenerated secrets and is single replica; replicaCount above one hard-requires Redis; chart tests cover rendering, secrets, HPA, networking, validation and drain cron jobs; Compose adds a Caddy overlay for automatic TLS; hosted community limits and S3 addressing style are explicit values.
verevonRelevance: Verevon planes already ship via GitOps; the explicit rule that a chart must not generate secrets under template-only rendering, plus validation that fails early, is a cheap safeguard to copy.
notes: Chart defaults are single replica with autoscaling off; HA values are shipped as fixtures and examples.

name: Client performance budgets measured under agent load
what: The desktop is tested for typing latency, scroll smoothness and channel switch long tasks while simulated agents flood typing indicators and live messages.
how: Playwright perf project (separate config, one worker, no retries) with tests that read the Event Timing API: typing-latency runs an identical 80 character burst under 4x CPU throttle in a quiet scenario and a busy scenario (8 agent pubkeys emitting typing indicators every 250 ms plus a live markdown message every 2 s) and reports median, p95, max and count of keystrokes over 50 ms; cold-switch and warm-switch tests count long tasks; scroll-smoothness and a scrollback test on a bug-heavy channel; only the quiet-versus-busy delta on one machine is treated as the signal.
verevonRelevance: Agent-busy rooms are where Verevon will feel slow first; encode a budget (keystroke latency and long tasks with N streaming agents) as a CI-visible benchmark before enabling push realtime.
notes: These are regression harnesses on mock data, not production telemetry; no field latency numbers were found in the repo.

name: Agent-led onboarding: welcome channel kickoff, starter channels and built-in personas
what: A new member lands in a Welcome channel where built-in agents greet them and introduce themselves, with starter channels and a welcome canvas already in place.
how: Onboarding feature (about 56 files) runs a kickoff stage: the Fizz persona posts an opener, teammate agents (for example Honey and Pollen) introduce themselves in-thread once their presence is observed, and a closer follows; starter channels are created by ensure_starter_channels; welcome canvas and guide modules seed content; machine onboarding handles the agent runtime check. The post-mortem record shows the design tension: the kickoff once decided from timers and produced announcements that were wrong, too loud (agents replying to each other) or too quiet.
verevonRelevance: A first-run Space that is not empty (starter room, introductions by a default agent, orientation canvas) answers the empty-state problem; derive each claim from observed state, as the post-mortem advises.
notes: Built-in personas are branded (bee-themed) and ship with the desktop; I did not audit the full onboarding flow beyond the kickoff module and persona definitions.
